I designed and engineered the interactive SVG map that powers Armed Forces Wellness Center locations on Warfighter Wellness. Three theaters — United States, Europe, Korea/Japan — had to be readable at a glance and accurate when a center is added, moved, or renamed.

I built a custom post type and ACF metaboxes as the source of truth, then drove the map from WordPress wp-json so editors update locations without touching illustration files. Custom SVG and JavaScript handle region switching, hit areas, and detail panels. It is cartography as a CMS component: the map is the product, the admin is the ops console.

I designed and developed the Why VCU? microsite for prospective students who were already drowning in viewbooks. The job was to make Virginia Commonwealth University feel specific: two campuses, a working city, a research and health system in the same breath as student life — and to do it with interaction, not a bullet list of rankings.

I built it in Terminal Four with custom HTML, CSS, and JavaScript: interactive modules that let a visitor poke at academics, community, and Richmond without a linear scroll to nowhere. It was recruitment as product design — motion and structure in service of a decision, not a brand film with a form at the end.
